c.tagline: Charlemagne's cathedral capital on Germany's tri-border corner with Belgium and the Netherlands.

taxi.fareNote: German taxis are legally required to run on the meter (Taxameter); flat rates are only common for pre-booked airport transfers.

emergency.note: 112 is the EU-wide number connecting to ambulance and fire services and works from any mobile phone, even without a SIM card.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Keep an eye on belongings around the Hauptbahnhof and bus station late at night and in Christmas-market crowds, where pickpockets work.

hood_desc: The compact medieval core around Aachen Cathedral, the Rathaus and Elisenbrunnen, packed with cafes, shops and museums; best for first-time visitors who want everything walkable.
The area around Aachen Hauptbahnhof and the Marschiertor gate, convenient for arrivals with chain hotels and easy tram/bus connections to the rest of the city.
A leafy residential district around the medieval Burg Frankenberg castle, appealing to families and those wanting a calmer, greener base a short walk from downtown.

water.note: Tap water is excellent quality and safe to drink everywhere.

transit.hours: Buses run roughly 5:00 AM to 1:00 AM, with a reduced weekend night-bus network filling in after midnight.
transit.pay: Tickets are bought from the driver, ticket machines, or the AVV/ASEAG app (eTicket); a regional day pass covers buses and trains across the Aachen area.
transit.note: Aachen has no tram or subway; ASEAG buses are the backbone of city transit, supplemented by regional trains at Aachen Hauptbahnhof for trips to Cologne, Liège and Maastricht.

train: International connections to Liège, Brussels and Paris
Regional trains (RE/RB) to Cologne, Düsseldorf, Liège and Maastricht

car.idp: Not required for EU/US licenses; recommended for others

transit.m: Train via Köln Hauptbahnhof to Aachen Hauptbahnhof (~70-90 min total)

tip.r: Rounding up the bill or adding roughly 5-10% for good service is customary, even though a service charge is already included in the price by law.

food.name: Aachener Printen
food.desc: Hard spiced gingerbread sweetened with beet syrup, protected by EU origin status; sold plain, nut-topped or coated in chocolate.

places.name: Nobis Printen

places.name: Leo van den Daele

places.name: Lambertz shop
places.note: Aachen gingerbread house founded in 1688, with tins and gift boxes to take away.

food.name: Sauerbraten mit Rosinensosse
food.desc: Rhineland pot roast marinated for days in vinegar and spices, in a dark sweet-sour sauce thickened with raisins and crushed Printen.

places.name: Aachener Brauhaus
places.note: Big rustic brewpub-style house serving Aachen specialities including Sauerbraten and Puttes.

places.name: Sauerbratenpalast

food.name: Reibekuchen

places.name: Markt weekly market

places.name: Gaststaette Postwagen

places.name: Gaststaette Postwagen
places.area: Markt, attached to the town hall

places.name: Zum Goldenen Einhorn
places.note: Historic house on the market square with regional cooking and terrace seating.

food.name: Aachener Reisfladen
food.desc: Yeasted tart shell filled with milky cinnamon rice pudding, sometimes with cherries - the Sunday cake of the Aachen region.

places.name: Nobis Printen cafes
places.note: Cafe branches of the Printen bakery sell regional tarts and cakes.

places.name: Markt bakeries
places.note: Traditional bakers around the square keep Reisfladen on the counter at weekends.

food.name: Poschweck
food.desc: Aachen Easter loaf studded with raisins and sugar cubes that melt into pockets; baked in the weeks before Easter and eaten with butter.

places.name: Leo van den Daele

places.name: Nobis Printen

places.name: Markt bakeries

food.name: Aachener Thermalwasser
food.desc: Hot sulphur spring water that made the city a spa since Roman times, still free to sip from the fountain at the Elisenbrunnen.

places.name: Elisenbrunnen
places.note: Neoclassical colonnade with public drinking fountains; the smell is part of the experience.

places.name: Carolus Thermen
places.note: Modern thermal baths fed by the same springs, with drinking fountains inside.

places.name: Buechel spring fountains
places.note: Historic hot springs bubble up in the lanes where the Roman baths once stood.

food.name: Local beer and Kraeuterlikoer
food.desc: Rhineland brewing on the Belgian border: fresh unfiltered lager and altbier in wood-panelled pubs, plus herbal Printen liqueur as a digestif.

places.name: Aachener Brauhaus
places.note: Large brewhouse pouring its own beer with the traditional food menu.

places.name: Domkeller
places.note: Long-running student and jazz pub, the classic first stop on an Aachen night out.

places.name: Pontstrasse pubs
places.note: The university bar street, a solid kilometre of taps, cheap and busy every night.

landmarks: Aachen Cathedral (Aachener Dom)
Charlemagne's 8th-century Palatine Chapel anchors this UNESCO-listed cathedral, where thirty German kings were crowned beneath its shimmering Byzantine-style mosaics and golden shrine.
Cathedral Treasury (Domschatzkammer)
One of Europe's most important church treasuries, glittering with Carolingian and Ottonian masterpieces including the Cross of Lothair and Charlemagne's golden bust reliquary.
Aachen Town Hall (Rathaus)
Built atop Charlemagne's palace ruins, this Gothic city hall dazzles with its coronation hall frescoes and replica imperial crown jewels overlooking the Markt square.
Elisenbrunnen
A neoclassical colonnaded pavilion where Aachen's famously sulphurous thermal waters flow from public fountains, celebrating the spa heritage that drew Casanova and Frederick the Great.
Carolus Thermen
A modern bathing temple fed by Aachen's hot mineral springs, where visitors soak in indoor-outdoor pools continuing a Roman spa tradition over two millennia old.
Ponttor
A massive 14th-century twin-towered gate, one of the best-preserved remnants of Aachen's medieval city walls, still guarding the student-filled Pontstrasse quarter.
Centre Charlemagne
The city's sleek history museum on the Katschhof square, tracing Aachen's journey from Roman spa settlement through Carolingian capital to modern border city.
Couven Museum
An elegant 18th-century townhouse re-creating bourgeois Aachen life with rococo interiors, historic pharmacy fittings, and the room where chocolate was first pressed locally.
Lousberg
A leafy hill on the city's northern edge whose lawns and obelisk-topped summit reward walkers with sweeping panoramas over Aachen's spires and the tri-border countryside.
Puppenbrunnen (Doll Fountain)
A beloved bronze fountain with movable jointed figures of a knight, professor, and market woman that children and visitors twist into new poses daily.

train.note: Every cross-border train uses Aachen Hbf, where the high-speed line from Cologne meets HSL 3 into Belgium; several platforms carry switchable overhead power so they can handle Belgian 3 kV DC as well as German 15 kV AC. Eurostar, the former Thalys, still calls at Aachen on the Paris-Brussels-Liege-Cologne-Dortmund run, and DB's ICE International works Frankfurt-Cologne-Aachen-Liege-Brussels, but the two fare systems are separate - book Eurostar on eurostar.com and the ICE on bahn.de, and do not expect one ticket to be valid on the other. The cheap way over the border is regional: Arriva's RE 18 to Maastricht, SNCB's RE 29 euregioAIXpress to Welkenraedt, Verviers and Liege, and DB's RB 20 Euregiobahn to Heerlen all take ordinary regional tickets. There are no night trains at Aachen, and since every crossing is inside Schengen there are no routine passport checks, though you should still carry photo ID.

intl.to: Brussels, Amsterdam, Paris, London, Prague, Warsaw, Milan, Barcelona & beyond

bus.note: Aachen has no coach station as such - long-distance buses use the stop at Aachen West station on Henricistrasse, about 2 km northwest of the Hauptbahnhof and a short city-bus ride from the centre. FlixBus lists roughly 95 directly reachable destinations from Aachen, unusually many for a city this size, because it sits on the Ruhr-to-Benelux and Ruhr-to-France corridors. Buy on flixbus.com or in the app; tickets are e-tickets scanned at the door and advance fares can start around 5 euros. Belgian and Dutch runs such as Liege, Maastricht, Brussels and Amsterdam are short Schengen hops with no border formalities, while the London coaches include a full UK immigration check at the Channel, so carry a passport.

ferry.note: Aachen is an inland city in the far west of Germany with no coast, no navigable river and no lake, so no passenger ferry of any kind operates there.

half.name: Cologne
half.blurb: Major Rhineland city dominated by its twin-spired Gothic cathedral, reachable by direct train in well under an hour.

half.name: Monschau
half.blurb: Fairytale Eifel town of half-timbered houses lining a narrow river valley, often called the region's prettiest village.

half.name: Maastricht
half.blurb: Lively Dutch university city on the Meuse with a bookshop set inside a Gothic church and vaulted Roman-era caves.

half.name: Liège
half.blurb: Walloon industrial city with a striking glass-and-steel train station and its own distinct style of Belgian waffle.
